patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Attends daycare three times per week.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No fever, rash in other locations, itching, or systemic symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the pediatric patient presenting with multiple skin lesions.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: “I’m a 2-year-old girl. My mommy noticed small skin-colored, bumpy spots on my belly that don’t hurt or itch, and some are on my arms and legs too.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any small, raised bumps on your skin that have a tiny indentation or a "dimple" in the center?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, doctor—some of the bumps on my belly, and a few on my arms and legs, have a little dimple in the middle. They don’t hurt and I don’t feel itchy.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you need to urinate more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor. I’m not going potty more than usual and I feel like my pee is the same as always.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or lacking your usual strength lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I feel like I have my normal energy, and I’m not weak or unusually tired.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any difficulty with dressing yourself or putting on your clothes lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I can move around like normal, and dressing doesn’t feel harder than usual for me.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores appearing specifically along the veins in your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—those bumps aren’t lined up along the veins in my arms. They’re more on my belly and some on my arms and legs, and they’re not sore or itchy.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itchiness on your skin?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor. I don’t feel itchy at all, and the bumps on my belly, arms, and legs don’t seem to bother me or hurt.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any pain or cramping in your calf muscles when you walk that goes away once you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—my legs don’t hurt or cramp when I walk, and stopping doesn’t make any pain go away because I don’t really have any pain with walking.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed if your stools have become unusually pale, light-colored, or clay-colored recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor. My poop looks like it always has—no unusually pale or clay-colored stools.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any weakness in your hands, or have you had any trouble gripping or holding onto objects lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—my hands feel normal, and I can grip and hold toys and other things just like usual. I haven’t noticed any weakness or trouble using my fingers.”
